defects.defect: The wave is not defined for the answer 'wait' on Q8 part 1, which is the review's own default. (a) Q8 is written as a condition for switching on the 07:00 schedule only. The steps before it in the same phase (one hand-started run on the real reader, and three hand-started digests read against Tony's inbox) already send real mail to the cloud model, and the lookup phase and Jordan's inbox phase do not name Q8 at all. The roadmap's S3 line says OpenAI's 30-day retention is handled before any private agent uses OpenAI. (b) With 'wait' the wave has no exit test it can pass and nothing the family would notice, for as long as OpenAI takes, and the notes make the web helper in wave B wait for wave A's sign-off, so all three waves stall on a third party.
defects.fix: Two sentences. In the morning-text phase: 'No run of the real reader over a real inbox, hand-started runs, the lookup and Jordan's inbox included, happens before Tony's go-ahead on Q8 part 1 or OpenAI's approval; until then every test uses the eval-only copy and the test mailbox.' In the wave's notes: 'If Q8 is wait, wave A stays open with only its schedule step and exit test left, and wave B, which needs nothing from A, is run and signed off first; A's exit test is run when the answer arrives.' Or make Q8 a condition for starting the wave A plan at all.

defects.defect: The roadmap's first rule after 'one new kind of risk per milestone' is 'private data arrives only after local models and egress controls are in place', and its S2 level (firewall blocking by default, outbound proxy enforcing, secret egress proxy) sits before the web milestone, which sits before mail. Wave A puts a whole inbox live behind one firewall rule and builds the rest of S2 in wave B, after mail is running. The list of departures Tony signs says only 'mail comes before web reading', and the Q11 line asks him only whether the rule and the planted-mail test stand in for 'the reader makes no network calls'. Nothing tells him that the blocking firewall, the proxy and the secret egress proxy arrive after his mail is being read, and no size is given for keeping the roadmap's order.
defects.fix: Add that sentence to the first phase's departure list and to the Q11 line in needs_from_tony, and add one line to the estimate: with the full outbound gate built first, wave B's gate phase without the device list (about 6 hours, 11 steps) moves into A ahead of the reader, A is then about 25.5 hours and 53 steps without the lookup, which is not one plan; it is one plan only if Tony waives the proxy (about 3 hours) or leaves the coded check for later (S1).

defects.defect: The outbound gate as written cannot be passed with the web helper working. The firewall rule gives the gateway 'its model, search and weather hosts', the proxy is 'an allowlist of model and connector hosts', and the phase's check is that 'one request to an unlisted host' is refused 'through the path page fetches will actually take'. A helper that reads public web pages must reach unlisted hosts. The F019 record says so itself: page fetches leave the gateway process directly unless a trusted-proxy switch is set (confirmed in the installed docs), the blocking firewall 'would have to allow that traffic', and once the helper has page fetch the proxy 'cannot double as an exfiltration allowlist; it can deny private ranges and named hosts and nothing more'. So after wave B the one gateway process, which also runs the mail readers and the parents' own agents, may reach any public address, and the exit test's 'all outbound traffic stayed inside the proxy and firewall rules' and the sign-off statement claim more than the gate can give.
defects.fix: Reword the gate check: 'an unlisted host is refused for the gateway's model and connector calls through the proxy; for page fetches only home-network addresses are refused (typed, by redirect and by name lookup), on the path the fetches take.' State in the phase and in the sign-off statement that from this wave the gateway process may reach any public address for page fetches, so tool permissions, not the firewall, keep the mail readers and the parents' agents off the web. Change the exit test's last clause to 'no connection to a home-network address and none from a program without a rule'.

defects.defect: The roadmap's S2 level names a Prompt Guard tripwire before web reading. The first phase offers Tony two choices, 'waive it, or schedule it with local models', and both leave it out of wave B; his call is not among the web helper's go-live conditions (those name only the proxy or its waiver and T4).
defects.fix: Add 'Tony's written call on the tripwire' to F019's condition and to the helper phase's go-live line, and add the third choice in words: 'if Tony wants it before web reading, the helper waits, because no card builds it'.

defects.defect: After this wave a parent's own agent holds private chat (and mail answers if the lookup is on), reads outside content directly (photos and PDFs) and holds the hand-off to a helper that fetches any public address: all three legs, with a prompt rule and planted tests between them. Tony's written yes is asked only for the lookup, and only 'if the lookup is live' at the first phase, which misses a lookup that slid from wave A and goes live in the second phase. The sign-off statement says only that the parent's agent 'still cannot browse or fetch' and is silent on attachments plus the hand-off.
defects.fix: Change the first-phase line to 'if the lookup is live or is built in this wave', and add one sentence to the sign-off's hard-rule statement: 'a parent's own agent now reads photos and PDFs (and mail answers, if the lookup is on) and can hand a task to the web helper; only a prompt rule and the planted tests stand between them, which is the leak path the roadmap names.'

defects.defect: Two pending simplifications are handled loosely. S15 is taken as settled: F083 says the snowfall figure 'is not built' and the helper's answer rule is S15's form, with no 'unless declined' branch, and S15 is missing from relies_on_simplifications. S13 is listed as relied on, but S13 as written parks F028 and F049 and folds waves C, D and later into one parked list, which Tony turned down on 12 Oct; a plain 'yes' to S13 would take F028 out of this wave. The 'emailed version' is also called an S13 cut although S13 does not list it (it needs F049, which is in wave C), and the day-out rule promises 'opening hours' although the place lookup that supplies them is cut.
defects.fix: Add S15 to the list with its branch ('snowfall figure and the scripted on-it and verdict format only if S15 is declined, about 2 hours more, the wave is then about 23 hours'). Replace 'S13' by 'the F028 line of S13 only; S13's main proposal is not taken, because the waves stay'. Say the emailed version waits for F049 in wave C, and word the rule 'opening hours where a page that could be read shows them'.

defects.defect: The wave's risk statement says of mail text that 'only that reader sees it'. The F051 record lists as unverified 'whether a parent's reply to the digest reaches an agent that can see the digest text'. If the 07:00 text is visible to the parent's own agent when the parent answers in the same thread, mail-derived text reaches that agent without the lookup and without Tony's yes, and in wave B that agent gains the hand-off to the web helper. No phase checks it.
defects.fix: Add one check to the wave A exit test, with no new build: after the 07:00 text carrying a planted mail has arrived, Tony replies 'what did your last message say?'; his own agent must not be able to quote it, and its session record must hold no mail text. If it can, record that as the same departure as the lookup, for Tony's signature, before wave B's helper goes live.

defects.defect: The phase 'Try it first, then write the rule' runs T7 (a reminder created from an iMessage turn) before any rule exists, and ends with 'No tool is granted to a real agent in this phase'. T7 needs the scheduling tool, which can name a web address as a job's destination, on an agent Tony can text. It is to be 'an agent that holds no memory', but by wave C the only agent bound to Tony's handle holds his chat history (and mail answers if the lookup is on), reads web results and attachments and has the hand-off. The two statements only agree if a throwaway agent is used, and the definition does not say so.
defects.fix: Name the agent: 'T7 runs on a throwaway agent with no memory, no accounts, no hand-off and no other tool, reachable from Tony's phone for the test only and removed afterwards', and change the last sentence to 'the scheduling tool is never granted, even for the test, to an agent that holds a person's data before the rule is live'.

defects.defect: If S1 is taken, the roadmap's coded check on who may call a person's account connector (section 1b) has no home in A to C. Wave A says S1 'would leave it for later'; wave C creates the plugin only 'if reminders are wanted' and gives it the reminder rule only. With S1 taken and Q6 answered no, mail runs for good on tool permissions alone, and the calendar connector is added to the agent that holds a parent's notes with no coded check and no written acceptance. Tony's written acceptance is asked only for the case where T5 shows the check cannot work.
defects.fix: One sentence in wave C's first phase and one in the calendar phase: 'whenever the house-rules plugin is first created, its first rule is the account-connector rule from wave A (T5's connector part permitting), and it is live before the calendar connector is granted; if the plugin is never created, Tony's written acceptance of one layer covers the mail and the calendar connectors.'

defects.defect: Part 3 of Q8 (may Happy keep and re-send the children's health details while Zero Data Retention is pending; default: not stored) is not among wave C's questions, although this is the wave where Happy first stores what it is told and sends it back to the cloud model in later chats, and the F041 card's own example is a child's allergy. The typed family facts, which are sent to the cloud model at the start of every chat, are also missing from the wave's list of new risks.
defects.fix: Add Q8 part 3 to wave C's needs_from_tony with its default as one instruction line and one line on the printed sheet ('until Tony says otherwise, do not ask Happy to remember a child's health details, and none are typed into the family file'), and add the typed facts to new_risks. No new mechanism.

defects.defect: F041 is marked 'Unconditional: remember this for both parents', and it is the only thing in wave C that does not hang on an answer, so the wave rests on it. The fact sheet records no request from Tony for saved notes and says nothing is known about what Jordan wants; the roadmap lists memory for each adult's own agent, but not as one of the rows marked as his decision.
defects.fix: Word the condition as 'on Tony's yes when the plan is written (default yes: it is the roadmap's memory for each adult's own agent); Jordan's agent gets it once T6 has passed for her as a non-owner and she wants it'.

defects.defect: Two 'no' branches have no size or place. If S14 is declined the full self-check bundle adds about 3 hours, which makes the wave about 26.5 hours, and nothing is named to give way (the S9 branch does name the lookup). If Q9 is answered 'Jordan needs her own stop', G005's in-house stop is sent to wave C as 'one more rule in the house-rules plugin', but wave C has no phase, hours or check for it, and a rule that only blocks tool calls does not stop a scheduled text.
defects.fix: Add to G008's condition 'and then the lookup phase moves to wave B'. For G005 either give the stop phrase a named phase in wave C with its size and its own check (the throwaway-job test the card lists), or say that on that answer it joins the not-in-a-wave list until Tony picks it.

size.basis: My estimate, not a measurement. Recount of the definition's eight costed phases at M1's rate (49 steps, about 20 hours): get ready 4 steps and 2 h (ten answers, the departures, a backup, T8), Google sign-in 7 and 3 h, scheduler switches and one firewall rule 6 and 3 h, mail reader with the coded check 11 and 6.5 h, morning text 7 and 3 h, paper and the daily sign-in check 4 and 2 h, lookup 4 and 2 h, exit gate 5 and 3 h. The definition's own figure is 22.5 h counted, shown as 23.5. It fits one plan only at the ceiling, only in the simplified form (S6, S9, S14; about 41 h as the cards are written, which is two plans), only for Tony's inbox, and only because Jordan's inbox (1.5 h, 4 steps) and the envelope (1.5 h, 3 steps) are outside it and the lookup can slide to B (then about 22.5 h and 44 steps). Without the coded check (S1) about 22 h. It cannot close before day nine, and it cannot close at all while Q8 part 1 is 'wait'. Mail reading (G015 with F051) is in this wave.

My estimate. Get ready 3 steps and 1 h, outbound gate 13 and 7.5 h (every existing program needs a rule and a re-check; the proxy runs in report mode before it enforces), web helper 10 and 5 h (the redirect and name-lookup cases need fixtures), photos and PDFs 5 and 2.5 h, hourly weather 2 and 1.5 h, day out 4 and 2 h, exit gate 5 and 3 h. The definition says 21 h. Fits with S7, the F028 cuts and S15 (about 31 h as written; about 23 h as written without the day-out phase). With Jordan's inbox arriving from A about 24 h and 46 steps. With all three pieces A may send (inbox, envelope, lookup: 5 h, 11 steps) about 27.5 h and 53 steps, which is over one plan until weather and the day out move to C; the definition gives that rule but never that sum. About 3 h less if Tony waives the proxy.

My estimate, with every main answer yes: get ready 3 steps and 1 h, T7, T5 and the reminder rule 5 and 3 h, typed facts and notes 11 and 5.5 h, reminders 7 and 3.5 h, dates from a flyer 2 and 1 h, calendar questions 6 and 3.5 h, evening text 3 and 1.5 h, exit gate 5 and 3 h. The definition says 21 h, shown as 22. Fits only with S5, S8, S10, S11 and the one-plugin shape of S1 (about 40 h as written). Only notes are unconditional, so the plan is anywhere from about 10 h and 20 steps to 22 h and cannot be written before Q6, Q4 and Q2 are answered. Weather and the day out arriving from B add 3 h and 6 steps (about 25 h, 48 steps, the top of one plan), and creating the plugin here adds 1.5 h if wave A went without it; 'email me this' (4.5 h) and the handbook folder (1.5 h) fit only in place of another phase.

Ran python3 over r7.json and merged.json: 42 ids, each once, 19 in waves and 23 not, none missing, none extra, none doubled; printed depends_on for the 19 placed items and checked each named item against its wave and phase order (every hard dependency is in the same wave earlier or in an earlier wave; the ones that point at G009, F031, F063 and the place lookup are cut by a named simplification, and F051's reminder offer and F028's calendar and email extras arrive later without anything waiting on them). Read the description, how, safety, caveats and unverified fields of the 19 placed items and of ten unplaced ones (MAC-02, OCL-01, G009, F043, F031, F030, F003, F006, AUT-06, G001), and the upheld review rows that mention gates, the proxy, retention or the hand-off. Per wave I listed each new kind of risk against the roadmap level it needs (A: S3 and the mail exit test, with S2 by the roadmap's order; B: S2 and the web exit test; C: the recipient test from S2 for reminders and email, T2 for the calendar sign-in) and walked the three legs of the lethal trifecta for the mail reader, the web helper and each parent's own agent after A, after B and after C. Checked every Q2, Q3, Q4 and Q7 item for a stated condition, and every S and Q number the definition leans on against its relies-on and needs lists. Checked two facts in the installed OpenClaw docs: that page fetches use direct routing unless the trusted-proxy switch is set (tools/web-fetch.md, cli/doctor/checks.md), and how scheduled announcements are delivered (automation/cron-jobs/delivery.md). What held: mail reading is in wave A; three waves and no fourth; each wave has one exit test and gives its size both ways as an estimate; the mail reader has no way out but its scheduled text; the web helper holds nothing; reminders and email are pinned in code to the asker before they are granted; no payment, booking, group chat or send into another person's conversation is added; Tony's two advanced examples are outside A to C and the notes tell him so. Not done: nothing was run on the Mac, the openclaw CLI was not used, no device was contacted, hours were not measured, and the 'as written' figures (41, 31, 40 hours) were not re-derived.
